cases.title: Contemplation, skill and action
cases.question: What does a person do in the selected teachings, and what conditions belong to that practice?
cases.reading: The selected Ra exchange proposes seeking love and recognizing the Creator in people, self and surroundings, grounded in meditation, contemplation or prayer. The Bashar excerpt presents a five-part project sequence: passion, project, preparedness, people and persistence. Both address personal orientation, but their practical sequences differ.
cases.conditions: Ra 10.14 is an explicit printed request for general practices; the Bashar highlight combines an introductory teaching with a later conversational example. Its preparation and collaboration conditions must remain attached to action on passion.
cases.counter_reading: Contemplation need not exclude action, and action on a project need not reject contemplation. These passages cannot rank either tradition as more active or passive overall.
cases.limitations: No shared audience question, behavioral outcome, therapeutic benefit or authenticated speaker is established. A685-word promotional excerpt cannot stand in for its complete paid session.

cases.title: Acceptance of desire and belief-based fear
cases.question: Are acceptance of difficult experience and changing fear-related beliefs the same instruction?
cases.reading: Ra 18.5 recommends understanding and accepting desires rather than suppression, while distinguishing imagined exploration from actions that violate its free-will framing. The Bashar excerpt explains fear through negative beliefs and proposes changing one’s relationship to perceived emotional frequencies. Both invite self-examination, but desire, fear and empathy are different constructs.
cases.conditions: The Ra passage explicitly constrains physical enactment of some desires. The Bashar example concerns a question about empathic feeling; its frequency language and claim of a physical mechanism are source claims.
cases.counter_reading: A shared introspective vocabulary can conceal distinct practices and different assumptions about why distress occurs. Acceptance does not mean endorsing every impulse, and this excerpt does not establish that all fear has one cause.
cases.limitations: No clinical efficacy or physical frequency mechanism is measured. The ASR’s alternating questions and replies do not independently identify speakers.

cases.title: Future-relative higher self and a single-moment account
cases.question: Do the selected uses of simultaneous time state the same cosmology?
cases.reading: Ra 36.4–36.6 qualifies the questioner’s simultaneity premise and describes a higher self as future-relative from human space/time. The Bashar excerpt’s opening treats time as changing viewpoints on one moment, then turns to guidance, relevance and acting on passion. Broadly similar vocabulary does not establish equivalent reference frames or taxonomies.
cases.conditions: The Ra answer explicitly changes perspective between an all-at-once account and human space/time. The Bashar practical passage limits fulfillment to what it calls relevant needs and includes action language despite its surrender metaphor.
cases.counter_reading: Reading only a sentence about the future or the present could manufacture a contradiction. The sources may be using different reference frames, but the passages do not supply a common formal model that resolves equivalence.
cases.limitations: These are attributed metaphysical accounts, not measured time travel or physics. Three contiguous complete Ra exchanges were read to retain the qualification.

cases.title: Conditional language is not a calibrated probability
cases.question: How should conditional future statements be preserved when comparing these recordings?
cases.reading: The Tracy opening defines the contact under discussion as visibly physical encounters and uses relative-year possibilities. The Pamela interview allows changing timelines but also makes specific election expectations, including repeated choices and possible election-day disruption. Conditional framing should be retained without erasing concrete assertions.
cases.conditions: The passages concern different events, audiences and publication contexts. The Pamela claims belong to a mixed interview; no diarization proves which utterance belongs to a purported council. A later portion of that interview explicitly changes to a different claimed speaker.
cases.counter_reading: Neither a confident date nor a conditional disclaimer alone provides a calibrated probability. Similar future-oriented language is not a shared prediction or a contradiction; an outcome audit would need frozen event criteria and exact dates.
cases.limitations: No forecast success/failure scoring or future safety advice is supplied. Baseline and Parakeet editions are separate; newly recognized wording is not inherited by old cards.

cases.title: Two Mother Mary labels, two trust referents
cases.question: Does advice about trust conflict with advice about personal boundaries?
cases.reading: The Natalie Glasson Mother Mary message frames distrust of the Universe or Creator’s support as disconnection from inner love. Pamela Kribbe’s Mother Mary message addresses highly sensitive people losing themselves in draining relationships and allows clearer boundaries or leaving. The immediate referents differ.

cases.limitations: The repeated printed name is not evidence of a common external speaker. Neither text’s psychological or spiritual effects are validated here.

cases.limitations: These two deliberately selected messages cannot establish the prevalence of either theme across a medium’s output or the identity of an attributed speaker.

cases.limitations: Compatibility is a narrow source-reading relation, not equal meaning, shared identity or efficacy of invocation.

cases.title: Attention during change and contemplative recognition
cases.question: What common practical element survives different religious or cosmological language?
cases.reading: The Michael message directs attention inward toward a supposedly stable core during rapid change, beginning with awareness of body and surroundings and breathing. Ra 10.14 proposes deliberate awareness of love and recognition of the Creator, with a contemplative foundation. A narrow common element is the recommendation to direct attention deliberately rather than merely react.
cases.conditions: The objects and claimed reasons for attention differ: an unwavering inner core in one text and love/Creator recognition in the other. The comparison does not merge those ontologies.
cases.counter_reading: Attention is a broad practice shared by many traditions. This parallel is too general to infer influence, common authorship or a shared source.
cases.limitations: The Michael body was read completely; only the selected Ra exchange was read for this comparison. No meditation outcome or religious truth claim is tested.

cases.title: A topic mention can be commentary rather than endorsement
cases.question: Why should skeptical reception and official highlights remain different source contexts?
cases.reading: The retained Ross and Carrie window recounts an interview and channeling performance, including a joke about a non-specific prediction. The official Open Contact highlight opens with disclosure framing but devotes most of its retained text to life lessons, free choice and a soul-school analogy. A shared Bashar/contact label conceals different genres and local content.
cases.conditions: The commentary is a second-hand reception account with unknown individual ASR voices. The official highlight is an edited publication with automatic captions; its title is not a full semantic description of every passage.
cases.counter_reading: Skeptical mention does not imply endorsement, while an official label does not authenticate a speaker or establish that all content concerns contact. Neither source should be reduced to title keywords.
cases.limitations: Only one fixed commentary window and one complete short highlight were inspected. This does not classify all remarks by either publisher or score a historical prediction.

cases.title: Skills, collaborators and community
cases.question: What limited practical overlap exists between these preparedness passages?
cases.reading: The Lyssa/Sasha excerpt recommends developing tangible skills and explicitly distinguishes community sharing from isolated hoarding. The Bashar Passion Principle excerpt includes learning relevant skills and collaborating with excited people before persistence. The limited shared proposition is that preparation can include skills and cooperative action.
cases.conditions: Lyssa’s source also contains economic and investment assertions presented as suggestions and individual choices; those are separate from the narrow skills/community overlap. The Bashar example concerns a project or career.
cases.counter_reading: Skills and cooperation are commonplace advice. They neither establish a shared channeled civilization nor validate the surrounding financial or metaphysical claims.
cases.limitations: This comparison is not investment advice, an outcome study, or a claim that both sources answered the same documentary audience question.

cases.title: A refusal, a reframed question and a correction
cases.question: When does a printed question fail to establish an affirmative answer to its premise?
cases.reading: Ra 68.9 declines an individualized density question under its first-distortion rule;68.10 answers a reframed generic hypothetical. Ra 77.15 explicitly rejects the questioner’s description before distinguishing kinds of intensity. These exchanges illustrate why prompt vocabulary cannot be treated as an endorsed answer.
cases.conditions: The shift from a particular person to a generic hypothetical matters. The77.15 qualification depends on the source’s interpretation of the question, and the corrected density comparison is not the same proposition as the refused 68.9 question.
cases.counter_reading: A refusal is not evidence of either agreement or disagreement with an unstated answer. A later hypothetical answer does not automatically license the originally refused personal inference.
cases.limitations: This is a documentary dialogue control, not validation of density categories or an explicit contradiction between two sources. Additional nearby Ra 68 exchanges were inspected and remain in the reading denominator.

reading_method.selection: Twelve purposeful candidates frozen before new ranking inspection; source title/known qualitative finding/repeated label and negative control criteria, not prevalence sampling.
reading_method.normalization: NFKC, strip outer whitespace, Python characters with exclusive end; exact body and span hashes.
reading_method.coverage: Union overlapping inspected intervals within an edition; canonical and additional ASR editions counted separately. Only the displayed passages were read here, not full audio listening.
reading_method.keyword_use: Literal first-distortion/intensity retrieval located selected Ra68/77 refusal/correction passages; all returned inspected complete exchanges remain in coverage, including unused contextual exchanges. Keywords locate passages, not semantic truth labels.

limitations: Twelve cases were purposefully selected before new ranking inspection; they illustrate interpretation and failure modes, not prevalence or a contradiction benchmark.
All comparison questions are analyst-authored. Actual printed Ra question IDs and inherited knowledge-bank question links are separately labeled.
No human annotation validation, acoustic listening, diarization, entity authentication, clinical/financial efficacy or forecast outcome evaluation was performed.
Canonical body hashes are checked; additional Parakeet reading is an alternative-edition inspection and excluded from primary-case and primary-word counts.
Repeated sources make the comparisons dependent. Zero explicit contradictions in this set would not establish their absence from the wider corpus.
Unreviewed publisher contexts and portions of partially inspected texts remain explicitly unreviewed. Computed topics and embeddings are not manual reading coverage.
Broad similarities can reflect common language, publisher editing, genre, source style, shared premises or sampling. No borrowing, common origin or scientific truth follows from resemblance.
